newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as wheat collapses late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as wheat collapses late.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on Friday, in line with sharp declines in wheat, with bearish fundementals noted, traders said.
"There's really no fundamental support for corn right now," a trader said. "Until we see something supportive in soybeans, don't expect much out of corn."
Wheat futures broke late amid renewed talk Egypt and India would look elsewhere for supplies to fill upcoming tenders. Nearby wheat futures touched fresh contract lows.
News South Korea bought 36,000 tonnes corn from China also weighed on the corn market.
China may export another 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes corn in the near future, grain officials there told Reuters.

Options trade was again active. Dean Witter reportedly sold 800 March $2.70 calls at 1-1/2. ADM sold 300 December $2.50 puts at 10-1/2. FIMAT Futures bought 400 March $2.70 puts at 3-1/2, traders said.
On the day, Rosenthal Collins sold five million bushels March, Tenco Inc sold two million March and Refco Inc sold 2.5 million July and one million March, traders said.
Corn closed 3-1/2 to 1/2 cents per bushel lower with March off 3-1/2 at $2.70-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 42,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 40,815 contracts.
